title: The package registry is Verdaccio serving double duty as an npm registry and an ESM CDN, transparently proxying and caching upstream tarballs
content:
`@powerhousedao/registry` is a Verdaccio-based registry that is also a **CDN for package bundles (ESM)**, so a browser or Node process can `import()` a package's built files directly.

The package API is three endpoints — `GET /packages` (all discovered packages, filterable with `?documentType=`), `GET /packages/by-document-type?type=…` (package names providing a document type), and `GET /packages/<packageName>` (one package, scoped names supported).

The CDN endpoint is `GET /-/cdn/<packageName>/<filePath>`. On first request it **fetches and extracts the tarball** from Verdaccio, looking for files in the package root and then `cdn/`, `dist/cdn/` and `dist/`. If the package is not published locally, **Verdaccio transparently proxies** metadata and tarballs from the configured upstream (`--uplink`, default `https://registry.npmjs.org/`), and the CDN extracts that upstream tarball into `cdn-cache/<pkg>/<version>/` exactly as it does a local one — including for `@powerhousedao/*` packages, where the registry prefers its local copy and falls back upstream.

Caching is keyed on the **shape of the request**, which is the part worth remembering: a version-pinned request (`<pkg>@1.2.3/…`) gets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, while a moving request (a dist-tag like `@dev` or `@latest`, or untagged) gets `public, max-age=60, must-revalidate`. A version-derived weak `ETag` is sent and a matching `If-None-Match` returns `304`. And when the **upstream metadata lookup fails** — as distinct from a genuine not-found — the endpoint serves the latest cached version if it has one and otherwise answers `503` rather than a cacheable `404`, so a transient upstream outage cannot poison a cache with a negative result.
